questions.stem: Public Sector Banks (PSBs) are reportedly building Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) parameters into corporate credit risk assessment. In this context, consider the following statements about PSBs and ESG disclosure norms in India. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: A bank is classified as a 'Public Sector Bank' when the Government of India holds more than 50 percent of its equity capital.
ESG disclosures for listed companies in India are mandated through an Integrated Reporting framework notified by the Reserve Bank of India.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: under the Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertakings) Acts, the Union Government must hold a majority (over 50%) stake for a bank to be a PSB. Statement 2 is wrong on two counts: mandatory ESG disclosure in India is done through the Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR), not 'Integrated Reporting', and it is notified by SEBI (for listed companies), not the RBI.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: PSBs integrate ESG parameters into companies' credit risk assessment
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional ownership criteria of PSBs and the SEBI BRSR framework; similar to UPSC 2022 prelims questions on regulatory bodies governing financial disclosure.

questions.stem: A rare Royal Bengal Tiger sighting at Odisha's Debrigarh Wildlife Sanctuary has revived plans for tiger translocation there. Consider the following statements regarding the institutional and legal framework for tiger conservation in India. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) is a statutory body constituted under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, as amended in 2006.
Every notified tiger reserve is required to have a demarcated core (critical tiger habitat) area and a buffer area.
Project Tiger was launched in 1973 and is administered by the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
The Wildlife Institute of India is a statutory regulatory authority empowered to grant mining and industrial clearances inside tiger habitats.
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: the NTCA was created by the 2006 amendment to the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972, and the Act mandates demarcation of core and buffer areas for every tiger reserve. Statement 3 is wrong because Project Tiger is administered by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (via the NTCA), not the Ministry of Tribal Affairs. Statement 4 is wrong because the Wildlife Institute of India is an autonomous research and training institute, not a statutory clearance-granting authority.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Rare tiger sighting gives hope to Odisha sanctuary looking to house big cats
questions.pyqLink: Tests statutory status of NTCA and core-buffer design under the Wildlife (Protection) Act; cf. UPSC prelims questions on Project Tiger and protected area categories.

questions.stem: Forest officials tracking the tiger that strayed into Debrigarh said its stripe pattern captured on camera traps would help confirm its source population. With reference to wildlife monitoring technology, which one of the following best describes this 'stripe-pattern identification' method?
options: It is a technique of extracting mitochondrial DNA from pugmarks found in soil to trace a tiger's maternal genetic lineage.

It is a photographic identification method that uses each tiger's unique and permanent stripe pattern, much like a human fingerprint, to distinguish one individual from another across camera-trap captures.
It is a satellite-based thermal-imaging census method that counts tigers from aerial surveys without using ground-based camera traps.
It is a whole-genome sequencing technique used to determine which tiger subspecies is present in a given forest patch.
questions.explanation: Stripe-pattern matching (the basis of tools like M-STrIPES used by India's tiger monitoring programme) works because each tiger's stripe pattern is unique and unchanging, allowing individuals to be told apart across camera-trap images over time and across landscapes. The other options describe genuinely different techniques (DNA pugmark analysis, aerial thermal census, genome sequencing) that are not what stripe-pattern identification involves.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Rare tiger sighting gives hope to Odisha sanctuary looking to house big cats
questions.pyqLink: Tests awareness of biometric/photographic identification technology used in India's All India Tiger Estimation; static syllabus link to wildlife census methodology.

questions.stem: The Supreme Court took up the relocation of the Central Secretariat Library on its own motion after a newspaper report. In this context, consider the following two statements.
statements: Statement-I: In the Central Secretariat Library matter, the Supreme Court took suo motu cognizance of a newspaper report without any party filing a formal petition.
Statement-II: The power of the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognizance of a matter is an express power explicitly enumerated in the text of Article 32 of the Constitution.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement-I is correct: the report describes the Court taking suo motu cognizance of a press report and directing the government to file an affidavit. Statement-II is incorrect because Article 32 guarantees the right to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of fundamental rights by an aggrieved party; the suo motu power is not textually enumerated there but has evolved judicially, often invoked alongside Articles 136 and 142.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Ahead of hearing in Supreme Court, Government sets aside space for Central Secretariat Library
questions.pyqLink: Tests the judicial (not textual) basis of suo motu cognizance, distinct from Article 32's writ jurisdiction; builds on UPSC's recurring Statement-I/II format on constitutional provisions since 2022.

questions.stem: The Central Secretariat Library, currently run by the Ministry of Culture, is being relocated ahead of the Central Vista redevelopment. Consider the following pairs of cultural/heritage institutions and the Union Ministry administering them. How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Only the first pair is correct, as confirmed in the government order relocating the library under the Ministry of Culture. The National Archives of India is also under the Ministry of Culture, not the Ministry of Home Affairs. Rashtrapati Bhavan is maintained by the President's Secretariat (with CPWD under the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs for upkeep), not the Ministry of Culture. The Indian Council of Historical Research functions under the Ministry of Education, not the Ministry of Home Affairs.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Ahead of hearing in Supreme Court, Government sets aside space for Central Secretariat Library
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional affiliation of cultural/heritage bodies, a recurring UPSC favourite (cf. UPSC 2023 pairs on reports/publishing bodies).

questions.stem: India has offered to help establish food corridors after the blocking of grain exports via the Black Sea during the Russia-Ukraine conflict. Consider the following statements about the Black Sea. How many of the statements given above are correct?
statements: The Black Sea is bordered by Ukraine, Russia, Georgia, Turkey, Bulgaria and Romania.
It connects to the Mediterranean Sea through the Bosporus and Dardanelles straits via the Sea of Marmara.
The Danube, one of Europe's major rivers, drains into the Black Sea.
The Crimean Peninsula lies on the northern coast of the Black Sea.
questions.explanation: All four statements are factually accurate: the Black Sea is bordered by exactly these six countries; it opens to the Mediterranean via the Bosporus-Marmara-Dardanelles chain; the Danube empties into it; and Crimea projects into it from the northern coast.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: India ready to help set up food corridors, says Ukrainian President Zelenskyy after phone call with PM Modi
questions.pyqLink: Tests physical geography of a sea repeatedly in the news (location, connecting straits, bordering states); similar to UPSC's recurring 'places in news' map-based questions.

questions.stem: Zelenskyy said India was ready to mediate in establishing food corridors amid Russia's blocking of Black Sea grain exports. Consider the following statements in this context. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Black Sea Grain Initiative was a UN- and Turkey-brokered arrangement that allowed Ukrainian grain exports to resume from Black Sea ports during the war.
India's declared policy during the Russia-Ukraine conflict has included official supply of lethal weapons to Ukraine.
India is a signatory to the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), 1982, which governs freedom of navigation relevant to Black Sea shipping disputes.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: the 2022 Black Sea Grain Initiative, brokered by the UN and Turkey, allowed resumption of Ukrainian grain exports. Statement 3 is correct: India ratified UNCLOS in 1995, which underpins freedom-of-navigation principles. Statement 2 is incorrect, as India has maintained a position of strategic neutrality and has not officially supplied lethal weapons to Ukraine, consistent with its calls for dialogue and offers of mediation/humanitarian support as reflected in the Modi-Zelenskyy call.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: India ready to help set up food corridors, says Ukrainian President Zelenskyy after phone call with PM Modi
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's neutral-mediator stance in the Russia-Ukraine war and UNCLOS membership, both static concepts behind recurring Black Sea/Ukraine news; cf. UPSC 2021 prelims on international conventions India has ratified.

questions.stem: With reference to anti-conversion laws enacted by Indian states, consider the following statements:
statements: Statement-I: Several Indian states have enacted laws that place the burden of proof on a person facilitating a religious conversion to establish that it was voluntary.
Statement-II: Article 25 of the Constitution guarantees an unqualified fundamental right to propagate one's religion, so such laws are constitutionally impermissible.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II is the correct explanation for Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II is not the correct explanation for Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.explanation: Maharashtra's anti-conversion law, effective from August 28, 2026, requires whoever facilitates a conversion to prove it was voluntary, confirming Statement-I. However, Article 25's right to propagate religion is not absolute; it is expressly subject to public order, morality, health, and other Part III provisions, and the Supreme Court (Rev. Stainislaus v. State of Madhya Pradesh, 1977) held that the right to propagate does not include a right to convert another person. So Statement-II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: No Bible camp this Diwali: Why small churches in Maharashtra are holding back
questions.pyqLink: Tests Article 25 (freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion) and its reasonable restrictions; similar to UPSC's recurring fundamental rights/restrictions questions.

questions.stem: Consider the following statements regarding India's tourism and hospitality sector:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: The Ministry of Tourism is the nodal central ministry responsible for formulation of national policies for the development and promotion of tourism.
In India's national income accounting, tourism's contribution to GDP is classified under the industrial/manufacturing sector rather than services.
Foreign investment in the hotel and tourism sector is permitted only through the government approval route and not through the automatic route.
India's Tourism Satellite Account is compiled by the United Nations World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) rather than any Indian agency.
questions.explanation: Only the first statement is correct; the Ministry of Tourism is indeed the nodal ministry, as reflected in large hospitality investments like the IHCL-Ambuja West Bengal expansion. Tourism is classified under the services sector, not industry, so statement 2 is wrong. 100% FDI is permitted in the hotel and tourism sector through the automatic route, so statement 3 is wrong. India's Tourism Satellite Account is compiled domestically (by NCAER for the Ministry of Tourism), not by the UNWTO, so statement 4 is wrong.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: Indian Hotels, Ambuja plan Rs 2,700-crore hospitality expansion across West Bengal
questions.pyqLink: Tests sectoral classification of tourism (services vs. industry) and FDI routes, a recurring static-economy theme in UPSC Prelims.

questions.stem: With reference to the global climate change regime under discussion at COP31 in Antalya, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: COP31 is held under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), which was adopted in 1992.
Unlike the Paris Agreement, the Kyoto Protocol assigned legally binding emission reduction targets only to developed (Annex I) countries.
The principle of 'Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities' (CBDR-RC) obliges all parties, developed and developing alike, to undertake identical mitigation commitments.
questions.explanation: The UNFCCC was adopted at the 1992 Rio Earth Summit, making statement 1 correct. The Kyoto Protocol indeed imposed binding targets only on Annex I (developed) countries, unlike the Paris Agreement's universal NDC-based approach, making statement 2 correct. CBDR-RC does the opposite of statement 3: it differentiates obligations based on historical emissions and capability, not identical commitments, so statement 3 is incorrect.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: Expert Explains | COP31: What's at stake at UN climate summit in Antalya
questions.pyqLink: Tests UNFCCC/Kyoto Protocol/Paris Agreement distinctions and the CBDR-RC principle, a frequently tested static climate-governance concept.

questions.stem: The scrutiny of advanced AI-chip transfers to China through third-country data centres has drawn attention to multilateral mechanisms governing dual-use technology exports. With reference to the 'Wassenaar Arrangement', which one of the following best describes it?
options: A binding World Trade Organization agreement that mandates uniform tariff rates on semiconductor imports among member countries

A multilateral export control regime under which participating states voluntarily coordinate controls on transfers of conventional arms and dual-use goods and technologies, including advanced semiconductors
A bilateral treaty between the United States and China establishing permissible limits on artificial intelligence chip exports
A United Nations Security Council sanctions mechanism targeting technology exports to specific proliferator states
questions.explanation: The Wassenaar Arrangement is a voluntary, non-binding multilateral regime in which member states coordinate (not mandate via treaty) export controls on conventional arms and dual-use goods/technologies, which is the backdrop to controversies like restricted AI chips reaching China via third countries. It is not a WTO tariff instrument, not a bilateral US-China treaty, and not a UNSC sanctions mechanism.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Behind Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair, lies a much bigger China controversy
questions.pyqLink: Tests knowledge of export-control regimes for dual-use/strategic technology, relevant to UPSC's pattern of asking about international regimes/groupings (cf. questions on NSG, MTCR, Australia Group).

questions.stem: Consider the following pairs of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) and the state they are primarily associated with:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Siddis are one of Gujarat's recognised primitive tribes, concentrated in Talala taluka of Gir Somnath district, so the first pair is correct. Toto is a PVTG of West Bengal (Totopara), and Great Andamanese is a PVTG of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, both correctly matched. Kolam, however, is a PVTG found mainly in Maharashtra and Telangana, not Madhya Pradesh, making the third pair incorrect.
questions.subject: History, Art & Culture
questions.sourceTitle: Meet the Siddis: Tribal Gujaratis from Kathiawad, natural athletes of African stock
questions.pyqLink: Tests knowledge of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups and their state distribution, a recurring tribes-and-culture theme in UPSC Prelims.

questions.stem: With reference to the upcoming Mangaluru-Bengaluru Vande Bharat Express, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: Mangaluru is a port city located on the Arabian Sea coast in the state of Karnataka.
The Mangaluru-Bengaluru rail route falls under the jurisdiction of the South Western Railway zone, headquartered at Hubballi.
This railway route passes through the Eastern Ghats, which run parallel to India's eastern coastline.
Complete electrification of this broad-gauge rail route was achieved in 2023.
questions.explanation: Mangaluru is indeed an Arabian Sea port city in Karnataka, and the route is operated by the South Western Railway zone headquartered at Hubballi, as stated in the report. However, the route to Bengaluru crosses the Western Ghats, not the Eastern Ghats, so the third statement is wrong. Electrification of this specific route was completed only in December 2025, not 2023, making the fourth statement wrong too. Hence only two statements are correct.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Mangaluru-Bengaluru Vande Bharat Express launch likely on November 13
questions.pyqLink: Tests physical geography (Western vs Eastern Ghats) and railway zone geography, recurring static-geography anchors for infrastructure news.

questions.stem: With reference to the system of government in Israel, consider the following statements:
questions.closing: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: Israel's President is directly elected by citizens and exercises executive powers similar to those of a Prime Minister.
The Knesset, Israel's unicameral legislature, consists of 120 members.
questions.explanation: Israel's President is a largely ceremonial head of state elected by the Knesset, not directly by citizens, and real executive power rests with the Prime Minister, making statement 1 incorrect. The Knesset is indeed a 120-seat unicameral parliament, as reflected in the coalition-formation arithmetic described in the article (67 of 120 seats), making statement 2 correct.
questions.subject: International Relations
questions.sourceTitle: Can Eisenkot unseat Netanyahu: Path ahead, and one major roadblock
questions.pyqLink: Tests comparative government structures (parliamentary system, ceremonial vs executive head of state), a recurring IR/comparative-polity theme.

questions.stem:
The Supreme Court recently upheld the reopening of an income-tax assessment based on an investigative report. In this context, consider the following statements regarding reassessment of income under the Income-tax Act:
1. An Assessing Officer can reopen a completed assessment only on the basis of "tangible material" indicating that income has escaped assessment.
2. A scrutiny assessment completed after detailed examination of a return is passed under Section 143(3) of the Income-tax Act.
3. The power to reopen a completed assessment lies exclusively with the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, not with the Assessing Officer.
4. Where escaped income is related to an asset located outside India, reassessment proceedings can be initiated within an extended time limit.
How many of the above statements are correct?
statements: An Assessing Officer can reopen a completed assessment only on the basis of "tangible material" indicating that income has escaped assessment.
A scrutiny assessment completed after detailed examination of a return is passed under Section 143(3) of the Income-tax Act.
The power to reopen a completed assessment lies exclusively with the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal, not with the Assessing Officer.
Where escaped income is related to an asset located outside India, reassessment proceedings can be initiated within an extended time limit.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct: courts require "tangible material" before reopening an assessment (as the SC reaffirmed in the Sabharwal case), Section 143(3) governs scrutiny assessments, and the Income-tax Act provides an extended time limit for reassessment where escaped income involves a foreign asset. Statement 3 is false because it is the Assessing Officer, not the ITAT, who exercises the power to reopen an assessment by issuing a notice.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: When can the Income Tax Department reopen a taxpayer’s assessment?
questions.pyqLink: Tests institutional knowledge of Income-tax Act assessment/reassessment provisions, a recurring static-current fusion theme similar to UPSC questions on tax administration and the Income-tax Act.

questions.stem:
With reference to the legal and economic framework of demonetisation in India, consider the following statements:
1. The power to declare a series of bank notes as no longer legal tender is derived from Section 26(2) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, exercised by the Central Government on the RBI's recommendation.
2. Following the 2016 demonetisation, India's currency-to-GDP ratio has permanently remained below its pre-demonetisation level.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The power to declare a series of bank notes as no longer legal tender is derived from Section 26(2) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, exercised by the Central Government on the RBI's recommendation.
Following the 2016 demonetisation, India's currency-to-GDP ratio has permanently remained below its pre-demonetisation level.
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is correct: demonetisation of currency notes is carried out under Section 26(2) of the RBI Act, 1934, which empowers the Central Government to declare any series of bank notes as no longer legal tender. Statement 2 is incorrect because, per RBI data cited in the article, the currency-to-GDP ratio has returned to around its pre-demonetisation level, not remained permanently lower, even as currency in circulation has more than doubled.
questions.subject: Economy
questions.sourceTitle: 10 years after demonetisation, cash remains king despite India’s digital payments boom
questions.pyqLink: Tests the statutory basis of demonetisation and the concept of currency-to-GDP ratio, similar to UPSC's recurring questions on RBI functions and monetary aggregates.

questions.stem:
COP31, the UN Climate Change Conference, is currently underway. With reference to the international climate change framework, consider the following statements:
1. The Paris Agreement (2015) legally binds all signatory countries to limit global warming to exactly 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.
2. The Conference of Parties (COP) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change is held annually.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Paris Agreement (2015) legally binds all signatory countries to limit global warming to exactly 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels.
The Conference of Parties (COP) to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change is held annually.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct: COP meetings are held every year, as reflected by COP31 following COP30, with COP31 opening in Antalya, Turkey. Statement 1 is incorrect because the Paris Agreement sets an aspirational goal of holding warming "well below 2°C" while "pursuing efforts" to limit it to 1.5°C through voluntary Nationally Determined Contributions, not a legally binding exact 1.5°C cap.
questions.subject: Environment & Ecology
questions.sourceTitle: COP31: Why climate summits still matter, even as the world misses its targets
questions.pyqLink: Tests the static distinction between the Paris Agreement's temperature goals and its non-binding NDC mechanism, a frequent UPSC theme on climate governance.

questions.stem:
A plea before the Supreme Court has sought to reopen the debate on gender identity versus biological sex. In this context, consider the following statements:
1. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 requires every applicant to undergo sex-reassignment surgery before being issued any certificate of identity.
2. In NALSA v. Union of India (2014), the Supreme Court held that discrimination on the ground of "sex" under Articles 15 and 16 of the Constitution includes discrimination based on gender identity.
3. The right to equality before the law under Article 14 of the Constitution is available to any person, not only to citizens.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
statements: The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 requires every applicant to undergo sex-reassignment surgery before being issued any certificate of identity.
In NALSA v. Union of India (2014), the Supreme Court held that discrimination on the ground of "sex" under Articles 15 and 16 of the Constitution includes discrimination based on gender identity.
The right to equality before the law under Article 14 of the Constitution is available to any person, not only to citizens.
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is correct and directly drawn from the NALSA judgment's reasoning cited in the article. Statement 3 is correct because Article 14 extends to "any person," unlike Articles 15, 16 and 19 which are partly citizen-specific. Statement 1 is incorrect because the Act allows a person to obtain a certificate recognising them as "transgender" based on self-perceived identity without surgery; surgery is relevant only if the person seeks a certificate as male or female.
questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.sourceTitle: Gender identity vs biological sex: How a new plea in SC seeks to reopen debate
questions.pyqLink: Tests the constitutional scope of Articles 14/15/16 and the NALSA judgment, comparable to past UPSC questions on fundamental rights and landmark judgments.

questions.stem: The controversy around Nvidia and the sale of advanced AI chips to China has drawn attention to export-control regimes for sensitive and dual-use technologies. Consider the following pairs of multilateral export-control regimes and their primary focus area:
questions.closing: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
pairs: Conventional arms and dual-use goods and technologies
Export control of nuclear and nuclear-related dual-use items
Export control of chemical and biological weapons-related materials
Export control of chemical and biological weapons-related materials
questions.explanation: Pairs 1, 2 and 4 are correctly matched: the Wassenaar Arrangement covers conventional arms and dual-use goods, the NSG governs nuclear and nuclear-related dual-use exports, and the Australia Group coordinates export controls on chemical and biological weapons materials. Pair 3 is incorrect because the MTCR (of which India is a member) controls missile and unmanned delivery system technology, not chemical/biological weapons materials, which is the Australia Group's domain.
questions.subject: Science & Technology
questions.sourceTitle: Jensen Huang's scandal exposes Nvidia's 'key-man risk'. What does it mean?
questions.pyqLink: Tests India's membership and the mandate of multilateral export-control regimes (NSG, MTCR, Wassenaar, Australia Group), a recurring static topic linked to strategic technology and AI-chip export news.

questions.stem: Mumbai airport's plan to shift flights to Navi Mumbai International Airport has brought attention to Thane Creek, which lies adjacent to the airport site. Which one of the following best describes this water body?
options: It is a man-made reservoir created by damming the Panvel river for the city's drinking water supply.
It is a freshwater lake formed in a volcanic crater and recognised as a biosphere reserve under UNESCO's Man and Biosphere Programme.
It is a riverine floodplain formed by silt deposition from the Ulhas river and was notified as a Ramsar wetland of international importance in 2022.
It is a tidal estuarine inlet of the Arabian Sea supporting mangrove forests and large flamingo congregations, protected as a Flamingo Sanctuary.
questions.explanation: Thane Creek is a tidal estuarine inlet separating Mumbai from Navi Mumbai, fringed by mangrove forests that support large congregations of flamingos; part of it is notified as the Thane Creek Flamingo Sanctuary. It is neither a man-made reservoir, a volcanic crater lake, nor a river floodplain, which makes the other options near-miss distractors describing different categories of wetlands.
questions.subject: Geography
questions.sourceTitle: Why Mumbai airport plans to shift flights to Navi Mumbai by destination, not airline
questions.pyqLink: Tests identification of estuarine/wetland ecosystems near Mumbai, in the style of UPSC questions on India's coastal wetlands and protected areas.
